results.message: VALVE ids consistent across ESP32 and control module
STEPPER ids consistent (feeder/distributor/spiral)
ESP32 UART configured at 115200 baud (115200 8N1)
ESP32 reads HX711 directly via GPIO35(DT)/GPIO32(SCK); Pi GPIO27(HX711_SCK) is separate circuit for Pi-side HX711 reading
ESP32 GPIO4=T1, GPIO5=T2 for bean detection IR break-beam; Pi also reads T1/T2 for camera triggering via GPIO interrupts
ESP32 uses manual indexOf() string parsing instead of ArduinoJson library. Commands with complex args may misparse. Consider adding ArduinoJson library.
MQTT topics follow consistent naming: sorter/{id}/action and roaster/{id}/action
BatchStats provides granular grade weights; FeedCommand grade_preference is a filter request (not a direct field mapping)
BatchFeedComplete includes dispensed_bins list (fixed in v1.8)
QoS levels appropriate: batch/feed=EXACTLY_ONCE (critical), batch/output=AT_LEAST_ONCE, status=AT_MOST_ONCE (frequent heartbeat)
status and batch/output use retain=True (new subscribers get last state)
ML pipeline class names map cleanly to DB BeanDefect enum (via upper())
Pi 4 INT8 inference 45ms << color detection budget 125ms. ML inference is not the throughput bottleneck.
Dual camera captures top+bottom image pair per bean. ML pipeline processes each image separately; fusion logic combines results (any defect → reject)
TFLite model file (sorter_001.tflite) must be generated from training pipeline and deployed to Pi before hardware testing. Currently only pipeline code exists; model must be trained on real hardware.
Control state machine (9 states) is separate from batch state (5 states). No direct mapping required — control state governs system, batch state governs data lifecycle.
BeanRecord includes all required fields for traceability: weight, density, moisture, color, defect, grade, timestamp
5 calibration types tracked: ['ad7746', 'color', 'density_fan', 'hx711', 'vibrating_feeder']. Each module should create CalibrationRecord on calibrate().
HealthMonitor logs all state transitions, faults, and alerts to system_events table with severity + details_json
12 REST API endpoints defined covering status, batch, calibration, health, beans, reports, and control commands
API routes delegate to SorterController methods. Database queries go through Database class. No direct GPIO/I2C access in API layer.
No authentication on REST API (localhost-only by design on Pi). Production deployment should add token auth or restrict to VPN. Consider: @requires_auth decorator for external access.
API should return 400 for bad requests, 404 for missing resources, 500 for internal errors, with JSON error body
HealthMonitor tracks 17 sensor baselines with noise thresholds, drift limits, and offline detection
HealthMonitor publishes 6-level alerts; Dashboard visualizes with color coding (gray→blue→green→yellow→red→darkred)
Uses linear regression on recent samples to predict drift direction. Accuracy depends on sample count (≥10 for stable prediction). May need tuning with real hardware data.
Dashboard updates at 5fps (200ms) vs bean arrival 833ms. Display granularity is sufficient for real-time monitoring.
Dashboard includes BeanSimulator (50bpm, 8% defect rate) for demo without hardware. Demo mode verified working in v1.23.
Throughput chart maintains 600-point rolling buffer (2min @ 5fps). Total memory: 600 × 2 floats ≈ 5KB — negligible.
Database uses SQLite WAL mode with thread-local connections (connection-per-thread pattern). Safe for multi-threaded dashboard + MQTT.
paho-mqtt on_disconnect callback spawns reconnect thread (5s delay, daemon=True). Clean disconnects (rc=0) skip reconnect.

E-Stop is hardware-level interrupt (EXTI GPIO) + software state machine. ESTOP state halts all motors/solenoids immediately. Reset required before recovering. Not a soft fault — physical intervention needed.

SorterMQTTClient.disconnect() calls loop_stop() + disconnect(). Database connections close on app exit. ESP32 firmware has heap monitoring (g_status.heap_free_bytes). No explicit __del__ cleanup found — recommend explicit close() calls.
Database and MQTT use datetime.now().isoformat() (local timezone). For cross-timezone operation (cloud sync), consider UTC + tzinfo. Currently consistent within Pi (local timezone).
